chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from 'Ubayd from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If a prayer misses you and you remember it during the time of another, if you know that if you pray the missed one, the other will be missed in its time, then start with the missed one, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says, 'And establish the prayer for My remembrance.' And if you know that if you pray the missed one, the one after it will be missed, then start with the one whose time you are currently in and make up the other.
And establish the prayer for My remembrance

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it is not harmful for a person to make up his voluntary prayers after the morning prayer until the sun rises, or after the afternoon prayer until the light of the sun changes by yellowing.

key_terms.اِصْفِرَارُ: Yellowing (of the sun's light, indicating time for Asr)

ai.seo_question: How to prioritize making up missed prayers when their times overlap with current prayers?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the jurisprudential priority between *qada* (making up) and *hadhir* (current) prayers, ensuring that the obligation of timely performance is not compromised by backlog. It reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the prayer window while accommodating the faithful who may have missed prayers due to valid excuses. The inclusion of the verse 'And establish the prayer for My remembrance' underscores that the act of prayer itself is the primary means of maintaining divine connection, whether in its prescribed time or as a make-up.
